title: Fractal frost

reference.source: Reference 14: fractal frost print, 736 × 1308 px JPEG
reference.note: held locally; this page carries statistics measured from it and none of its pixels

summary: One escape-time field: the smooth escape count picks a color from a cyclic ramp, the exit angle draws field-line filaments at a held spacing, and the slowest pixels are the speckled ground.
units: reference pixels; the plate is 736 × 1308 and every length scales with the canvas

zoom.does: Width of the window on the plane. Smaller is deeper into the branches.

rot.does: Turns the window, so the branches leave the plate at other angles.

panX.does: Moves the window across, in window widths.

ground.does: Share of pixels slow enough to be ground.

cycle.does: How many times the ramp repeats per e-fold of escape count.

spread.does: Power on the log escape count before the ramp; above 1 the frost band near the ground widens and the far bands close up.

rim.does: Width of the turquoise rim where the frost meets the ground.

spacing.does: Target distance between field lines; the line count per turn doubles or halves to hold it.

bold.does: Share of field lines, picked per line, that print as bold white filaments.

lineW.does: Share of a bold line's period that prints white.

striate.does: Light and dark streaks of the ramp color along every field line.

feather.does: How far the band edges move along the field lines, so bands meet in interlocking fingers.

breaks.does: Noise on the cut level, so filaments break and swell along their length.

waver.does: Phase noise that bends the filaments sideways.

fur.does: Strength of the strands in the frost next to the ground, where the field lines are too dense to draw one by one.

furW.does: Cell size of the noise that the strands are smeared from: the strand width.

warp.does: Displacement of the plane before iteration.

kink.does: Share of ridged noise in the warp; ridges bend lines at a point.

pale.does: Width of the per-pixel draw across slate, steel, periwinkle and pale. 0 is a flat periwinkle.

speck.does: Strength of the navy specks where the iteration never leaves.

phase.does: Position along the loop: the ramp cycles once outward and the warp drifts 1.5 warp scales across.

seed.does: Re-rolls the warp and nudges the window.

modes.saw: value up to value + amp over period seconds, then again
modes.drift: seeded walk, one step of up to amp every period seconds, folded back at the slider ends

motion.runs: only while Motion is on, at half scale; the sliders hold the center values; off by default

live.runs: only while Live is on: a drag on the figure sets x across and y down between these ends; off by default

techniques.name: Grain
techniques.implementation: Ground arm: the slowest 20 % of pixels, a per-pixel draw through slate, steel, periwinkle and pale; navy specks gather in 3 px rosettes where the orbit never leaves.

techniques.name: Edge
techniques.implementation: Star crossing: several ground arms meet at a branch point of the set; the reference arms measure 12 px median and 29 px at p90.

techniques.name: Pull
techniques.implementation: Royal band: navy and royal striations every 4.6 px, every second line printed bold white where a 26 px noise allows.

pass_order: window: a 0.03-wide square of the parameter plane near a branch point of the Mandelbrot set, displaced before iteration by stretched value noise with a ridged part (13 px, 22 px scale), so the band edges and field lines kink
escape: z → z² + c to a bailout of 10^10; the smooth count μ, log|z| and the angles of z_n, z_n−1, z_n−2 and z_n−3 are kept; a coarse pass sets the count that makes 20 % of pixels ground
line density: |∇μ| is blurred 3 px; with log|z| it gives |∇θ|, and the level J = log2(2π / (4.6 px · |∇θ|)) picks the line set per pixel, blended between ⌊J⌋ and ⌊J⌋ + 1
ramp: d = 1.3 · (log μ0 − log μ)^1.5, read on a 12-stop cyclic ramp; the ramp position moves with the field-line phase so band edges meet in fingers; a turquoise rim at d < 0.028
filaments: every field line striates the band color; every second line, gated by a 26 px noise, prints bold, white on dark bands and royal on light ones
frost fur: where field lines are too dense to draw, a 2 px value noise is smeared 2 × 6 px along ∇μ and lit from the upper left
ground: a per-pixel draw through slate, steel, periwinkle and pale, darkening where the orbit stays longer, with navy specks gathered in 3 px rosettes; 6 levels of grain over everything

ramp_9_means.method: k-means, k = 9, on every second pixel; color and plate share

ramp_order.sequence: ground, turquoise rim, white frost with pale fur, slate, royal with navy, turquoise, mint, white filament field
ramp_order.method: nearest-class transects from the ground network into the four large flowers

filament_spacing_px.method: peak spacing (prominence 15) along the structure-tensor gradient in six 96 to 128 px patches

lobe_scale_px.method: class masks smoothed 9 px, opened twice; skeleton widths and component sizes

measured.rejected: a pure noise-blob composition: it gave no star crossings in the ground network and no field-line fans; an escape-time field gives both

benchmark.computed: live, when this page loads, by the code that measured the reference: default parameters, Frost palette, 1× reference size

setup.note: The window on the set is the plate's own, so no region lines up with the reference. Each render rect was chosen with search.py and a full-metric check among regions of the same material: ground arms with rosettes, a frost lobe beside the ground, a blue band with bold filaments, and a second-cycle white field.

limits: Bench mean 0.928, short of 0.98. The lowest metrics are the frost-lobe and white-field spectra and histograms (0.77 to 0.85): the reference frost is a JPEG-softened relief filter whose whites spread from L 200 to 250, and the plate's frost sits on a two-stop plateau near L 225 to 235 with a lit strand field on top. No blur was added to close it.

The ground patch autocorrelation (lag 2 to 6 near 0 in the reference) still reads 0.1 to 0.3 on the plate, because the plate's navy rosettes cluster on a 3 px field. Removing the clustering scored higher and read as flat noise at 1x.

Whole-plate shares follow the window: the plate puts 25 % of pixels in white against 16 % in the reference because its largest bay is white. The window is the plate's own; the reference's four flower heads are not traced.
The reference is a downscaled render with a relief filter. The plate builds the relief from the field itself (strands lit from the upper left, bold lines with a dark side), not from an emboss filter.
notes: Deterministic: the same palette, parameters and seed give the same pixels.
A display render is capped at 2.4 megapixels; a slider in motion draws at half scale (down to a quarter on a heavy engine) and the release redraws in full.
This spec follows the controls: open it again, or leave it open, after changing them.
